registry: Mempool Surf Club Explore — Marketplaces Research Registry
scope: Research and registry data only; no public Explore implementation, route, Shopify, Atlas, Learn, Home or Tools changes are authorized.

reference_schema.note: Marketplaces reuses the approved 24-field contract and validation semantics, not the Ordinals topic taxonomy.

required_fields: Why it matters in the Bitcoin marketplace ecosystem

status_definitions.ACTIVE: Current marketplace, protocol, operator, or materially relevant service operation was verified as of the record verification date.
status_definitions.HISTORICAL: The relevant marketplace/product phase is finite, completed, legacy, or no longer currently offered, but remains ecosystem-significant.
status_definitions.INACTIVE: Operation ceased, was abandoned, or became unsafe/unavailable without a verified active successor operation.
status_definitions.UNCERTAIN: Lifecycle/activity status itself cannot be determined from reliable evidence.

source_confidence_definitions.HIGH: First-party or primary evidence supports identity and core claims, including lifecycle where applicable.
source_confidence_definitions.MEDIUM: Credible evidence exists, but one or more core fields rely on archival, independent, incomplete, stale, or technically ambiguous first-party evidence.
source_confidence_definitions.LOW: Core attribution, scope, mechanics, or lifecycle evidence remains materially indirect.

source_hierarchy: Official GitHub, blog, support center, changelog, or official social account
Primary transaction/protocol documentation where marketplace mechanics depend on it
Market-data/indexer sources as supporting evidence only
_schema.one_entity_one_profile: One canonical entity = one canonical profile. Asset types, protocol support, wallet integrations, child products and collection listings are modeled as characteristics/relationships unless materially distinct canonical products require Command Center approval.
_schema.custody_rule: Do not infer non-custody from PSBT use, wallet-side signing, or absence of stored private keys alone. Describe exactly what users, scripts, pool wallets, platform services, and transaction builders control.
_schema.consensus_rule: Marketplace listings, order state, collection labels, rare-sat labels, BRC-20/Runes interpretation and metadata are not automatically Bitcoin consensus state.

topic_architecture.purpose: Canonical end-user venues where Bitcoin-native or Bitcoin-relevant assets are listed, auctioned, bid on, or purchased.
Trading protocols and marketplace infrastructure whose mechanics materially shape Bitcoin asset liquidity without fitting a conventional listing venue.

company_product_consolidation_decisions: Magic Eden: one MARKETPLACES record for the Bitcoin implementation; Ordinals and Runes are not split into separate profiles. Status is HISTORICAL for the Bitcoin implementation, not for Magic Eden as a company.
UniSat: one Marketplace product record with explicit WALLETS relationship; do not create separate profiles for each supported protocol or for UniHexa without Command Center approval.

Ordinals Wallet: one combined wallet/marketplace entity record here because the marketplace is a substantial canonical product; Master Explore must coordinate canonical-home/dedup behavior with WALLETS.
OKX: record is scoped to the Web3 Wallet Bitcoin marketplace, not the centralized exchange order book; link to EXCHANGES and WALLETS rather than conflating custody models.
Binance: one historical corporate/product record consolidates the 2023 Binance NFT Bitcoin phase and later Web3 Wallet Inscriptions Marketplace while explicitly preserving their different mechanics.
Gamma: one profile for its Bitcoin art marketplace/creator platform; no separate launchpad versus secondary-market profile.

Trio / OrdinalsBot: one combined profile covers the live Trio consumer marketplace and directly underlying OrdinalsBot marketplace/API infrastructure; do not create separate company and marketplace profiles without a master-registry canonical-home decision.

researched_omission_decisions.reason: Ord.io is canonically an Ordinals explorer/indexer rather than a marketplace. Its associated Zap trading product and Ord.io shut down on June 1, 2026; a marketplace record would mis-home the explorer and duplicate a discontinued adjacent product.

Current first-party positioning is a Bitcoin treasury/rare-sat hunting and data/API business rather than a multi-sided marketplace. Selling its own sourced sats does not establish a canonical marketplace venue.

First-party docs verify an early Bitcoin on-chain art and launch platform launched February 10, 2023, but the reviewed current material does not establish a durable secondary-marketplace role or verifiable 2026 trading operation.
Official product documentation is Solana-focused; no materially significant Bitcoin marketplace implementation was verified.

Xverse is canonically a wallet/aggregation surface. Its Rune swap flow routes quotes to providers such as UniSat, OKX and DotSwap; those venues are represented directly and Xverse is modeled relationally under WALLETS.
The site states that it is powered by Magisat API. Magisat is the underlying canonical rare-sat marketplace/infrastructure entity, so a second profile would be derivative duplication.

Emblem Vault is cross-chain vault/wrapping infrastructure rather than the canonical end-user Ordinals venue in this registry. Its material marketplace role is preserved in the Ordinals Market record and related-entity notes.
Marketplace aggregation/routing does not add a distinct canonical trading venue where underlying marketplace entities are already represented.
Canonically an indexer/data/analytics layer rather than a marketplace. Listing/market data should not create a duplicate MARKETPLACES profile.
Primarily a mint/launch/issuance tool in the reviewed scope; insufficient evidence for a distinct secondary-marketplace canonical profile.
Primarily wallet/trading aggregation infrastructure rather than a standalone marketplace venue in the reviewed scope.
UniSat describes UniHexa as a newer/beta trading engine. It remains under the UniSat canonical entity until Command Center determines it is a materially distinct product deserving a separate profile.
Testnet/incomplete evidence did not meet the canon threshold for current operational significance.
Insufficient first-party architecture, durable significance, or distinct historical role; including them would turn the registry into directory padding.
Reviewed current/historical material supports an inscription tool, ecosystem map, research and discovery role; a distinct durable marketplace/trading venue was not verified.

public_copy_caution_queue.reason: Do not reduce its custody model to a single adjective. Terms disclaim custody/private-key access, while current listing APIs use a scripted listing escrow output, service-built PSBTs and pre-signed recovery.
First-party sources confirm marketplace/launchpad operation and no private-key storage, but low-level transaction/custody architecture was not sufficiently documented.
One record spans two Binance product phases with materially different custody/user-flow assumptions.
Contemporary sources establish both Emblem Vault/Ethereum trading and reported PSBT adoption; exact transition/parallel-path chronology remains unresolved.
Historical domain compromise creates link-safety concerns; do not publish the old domain as an official call-to-action.
Repository reachability is not evidence of current operation; classify as HISTORICAL.
Marketing language around decentralization/self-custody must be qualified by documented pool-wallet control and fee-wallet mechanics.
